cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: one at a time · /wʌn æt ə taɪm/ · phrase · Phrase · New
Separately, with one person or thing followed by another. Get on the bus one at a time.
catch a bus · /kætʃ ə bʌs/ · phrase · Phrase · New
To get on a bus in time to travel on it. We can catch a bus at ten.
get on · /ɡɛt ɑn/ · phrase · Phrase · New
To enter a bus, train or similar vehicle. Get on the bus at this stop.
get off · /ɡɛt ɔf/ · phrase · Phrase · New
To leave a bus, train or similar vehicle. Get off at the next stop.
wait in line · /weɪt ɪn laɪn/ · phrase · Phrase · New
To wait behind other people until it is your turn. Please wait in line for the bus.
Recall and use
Cover the words. Say three from memory. Make a new sentence with one, then check the example.

cards.title: Read and write
sections: Reading

Heart and Puck plan to catch a bus. They wait in line at the bus stop. People get on one at a time. Heart asks the driver where to get off. The driver says the library is beside the next stop. They say thank you.
Find the answer
How do people get on the bus, and where do Heart and Puck need to get off?
Write
Write two sentences using two words from today’s new word bank.
